```{=html}
<div class="lx-case">
<div class="lx-case-part"><p class="lx-eyebrow">1 · The puzzle</p><p>An <span class="lx-term" data-term="electrolyzer">electrolyzer</span> next to a wind farm turns spare wind into hydrogen. When extra capacity runs fewer hours, a bigger one makes each kilogram cost more. Can the bigger one still be the better choice?</p></div>
<div class="lx-case-part"><p class="lx-eyebrow">2 · The question in one sentence</p><p class="lx-case-q">How do electrolyzers, hydrogen storage and <span class="lx-term" data-term="fuel-cell">fuel cells</span> change the cost, <span class="lx-term" data-term="curtailment">curtailment</span> and <span class="lx-term" data-term="firm-output">firm output</span> of a grid-connected wind farm?</p><p class="lx-hint">Question type: prescriptive (what should be built, and how should it run?).</p></div>
<div class="lx-case-part"><p class="lx-eyebrow">3 · Scale and boundary</p><ul><li><b>Inside:</b> one planned 253 MW wind farm in West Texas, with a battery and hydrogen equipment, hour by hour for a year (8,760 hours).</li><li><b>Left out:</b> the rest of the grid, which enters only through <span class="lx-term" data-term="ercot">ERCOT</span> <span class="lx-term" data-term="wholesale-price">wholesale prices</span>, and final federal hydrogen credit rules; costs date from 2020 to 2023.</li></ul></div>
<div class="lx-case-part"><p class="lx-eyebrow">4 · Decisions, goal and rules, in words</p><ul><li><b>Decisions:</b> the sizes of the battery, electrolyzer, hydrogen tank and fuel cell, and how each runs every hour.</li><li><b>Goal:</b> the lowest <span class="lx-term" data-term="life-cycle-cost">life-cycle cost</span> of the whole system, net of what it earns from electricity and hydrogen.</li><li><b>Rules:</b> deliver the largest steady output it can in every hour; no machine runs above its size.</li></ul></div>
<div class="lx-case-part wide"><p class="lx-eyebrow">5 · Data and method</p><ul><li>A <span class="lx-term" data-term="mixed-integer-program">mixed-integer linear program</span>, an extension of NREL's REopt model, sizes and runs the equipment over a year of hours with ERCOT wholesale prices.</li><li><span class="lx-term" data-term="sensitivity-analysis">Sensitivity runs</span> vary the hydrogen price, the wind profile (four regions) and projected equipment costs to 2050.</li></ul></div>
<div class="lx-case-part wide"><p class="lx-eyebrow">6 · What came out, and where it holds</p>
<blockquote class="lx-excerpt" data-source="excerpt:wind-hydrogen"><p>As the hydrogen price rose, the optimizer built a larger electrolyzer to use more surplus wind.</p><p>The larger unit ran at lower <span class="lx-term" data-term="capacity-utilization">utilization</span>, so each kilogram carried more <span class="lx-term" data-term="capital-cost">capital</span> and the <span class="lx-term" data-term="lcoh">levelized cost of hydrogen</span> rose, while hydrogen revenue lowered total system cost.</p><p>Compared with wind and a battery alone, adding an electrolyzer reduced total system cost by about 7%, and using hydrogen as the storage medium for fuel cells reduced it by about 26%.</p><footer>From: Li et al. (2024), <a href="https://doi.org/10.1115/1.4063971">Journal of Mechanical Design</a>.</footer></blockquote>
<p class="lx-hint">Battery, hydrogen and hybrid storage were compared, each set to deliver the largest <span class="lx-term" data-term="firm-output">stabilized output</span> in every hour at the lowest life-cycle cost.</p>
<p class="lx-hint">Hybrid hydrogen and battery storage delivered the highest stabilized output of the four configurations.</p>
<p class="lx-hint">Holds when: one planned West Texas wind farm, ERCOT prices, costs from 2020 to 2023. Leaves out: final federal hydrogen credit rules.</p></div>
<div class="lx-case-part"><p class="lx-eyebrow">Related study · solar and hydrogen</p>
<blockquote class="lx-excerpt" data-source="excerpt:solar-hydrogen"><p>Among the cases studied, <span class="lx-term" data-term="concentrated-solar">concentrated solar power</span> with <span class="lx-term" data-term="thermal-storage">thermal storage</span> running a <span class="lx-term" data-term="high-temperature-electrolyzer">high-temperature electrolyzer</span> at variable power gave the lowest levelized cost of hydrogen; constant-power operation was the most expensive.</p><footer>From: Li et al. (2023), <a href="https://doi.org/10.1109/EEM58374.2023.10161786">EEM 2023</a>.</footer></blockquote>
<p class="lx-hint">Yardstick here: the cost per kilogram across designs. Holds for: one West Texas site, cost projections from NREL's Annual Technology Baseline, a conference-length study.</p></div>
<div class="lx-case-part"><p class="lx-eyebrow">Related study · maintenance offshore</p>
<blockquote class="lx-excerpt" data-source="excerpt:offshore-om"><p><span class="lx-term" data-term="prognostics">Prognostics</span>-based maintenance lowered wind operation-and-maintenance cost by about 10% and downtime by about 11%.</p><p>The saving applies to the turbines alone, so its effect on the whole system was smaller: the levelized cost of hydrogen fell by about 2%.</p><footer>From: Li et al. (2024), <a href="https://doi.org/10.1088/1742-6596/2767/6/062016">J. Phys.: Conf. Ser. 2767</a>.</footer></blockquote>
<p class="lx-hint">Prognostics: predicting failures to plan repairs. Holds for: one Gulf of Mexico site and one weather year.</p></div>
</div>
<div class="lx-interactive" data-learn="cf2" data-src="../assets/learn/data/cf2-cost-per-kg-vs-system-cost.json">
```

## The idea behind it, then where the result holds
:::

```{=html}
<div class="lx-interactive" data-learn="cf2-idea" data-src="../assets/learn/data/cf2-cost-per-kg-vs-system-cost.json">
<div class="lx-fallback">
<!-- cf2-idea:start (written from the toy model by the test's --write mode; do not edit) -->
<p class="lx-eyebrow">Your electrolyzer, one 10 MW block at a time (illustrative)</p><table class="lx-facts cf2-assume"><caption class="lx-hint">The toy's assumptions (illustrative)</caption><tbody><tr><th scope="row">Electricity</th><td>free in this toy: it is surplus wind the grid cannot take, which would otherwise be curtailed</td></tr><tr><th scope="row">Full-power hours</th><td>fewer for each added block: it runs only when the surplus is larger than the blocks below it</td></tr><tr><th scope="row">Building cost and fixed upkeep</th><td>$140,000 per MW a year (annualized)</td></tr><tr><th scope="row">Hydrogen per MWh</th><td>18 kg (about 55 kWh per kg)</td></tr><tr><th scope="row">Water and stack wear</th><td>$0.20 per kg</td></tr></tbody></table><p class="lx-hint">Worked block: 10 MW × 5,000 h × 18 kg/MWh = 900,000 kg a year. It costs $140,000 × 10 + $0.20 × 900,000 = $1,580,000 a year, so $1.76 per kg.</p><p class="lx-hint">Net cost change below zero: the system saves money compared with no electrolyzer.</p><table class="lx-facts"><caption class="lx-hint">Each 10 MW block of the electrolyzer: the hours it runs at full power and its own cost per kilogram.</caption><thead><tr><th scope="col">Block</th><th scope="col">Full-power hours a year</th><th scope="col">Hydrogen, kg a year</th><th scope="col">Its cost per kg</th></tr></thead><tbody><tr><td>0–10 MW</td><td class="n">5,000</td><td class="n">900,000</td><td class="n">$1.76</td></tr><tr><td>10–20 MW</td><td class="n">4,200</td><td class="n">756,000</td><td class="n">$2.05</td></tr><tr><td>20–30 MW</td><td class="n">3,500</td><td class="n">630,000</td><td class="n">$2.42</td></tr><tr><td>30–40 MW</td><td class="n">2,900</td><td class="n">522,000</td><td class="n">$2.88</td></tr><tr><td>40–50 MW</td><td class="n">2,400</td><td class="n">432,000</td><td class="n">$3.44</td></tr><tr><td>50–60 MW</td><td class="n">2,000</td><td class="n">360,000</td><td class="n">$4.09</td></tr><tr><td>60–70 MW</td><td class="n">1,600</td><td class="n">288,000</td><td class="n">$5.06</td></tr><tr><td>70–80 MW</td><td class="n">1,300</td><td class="n">234,000</td><td class="n">$6.18</td></tr></tbody></table><ul><li>At $3.00/kg the system's net cost is lowest at <b>40 MW</b> (−$2.26M a year against no electrolyzer), where the hydrogen costs $2.19/kg on average.</li><li>At $4.00/kg the system's net cost is lowest at <b>50 MW</b> (−$5.31M a year against no electrolyzer), where the hydrogen costs $2.36/kg on average.</li><li>At $5.00/kg the system's net cost is lowest at <b>60 MW</b> (−$8.88M a year against no electrolyzer), where the hydrogen costs $2.53/kg on average.</li><li>The lowest cost per kilogram is always the smallest size, 10 MW ($1.76/kg), whatever the price.</li></ul>
<!-- cf2-idea:end -->
</div>
</div>
<div class="lx-xcard">
<header class="lx-x-head"><h3>Two numbers, two questions</h3></header>
<table class="cf-two">
<thead><tr><th scope="col">Measure</th><th scope="col">How it is built</th><th scope="col">The question it answers</th><th scope="col">Best size in the toy at $4.00/kg</th></tr></thead>
<tbody>
<tr><th scope="row">Cost per kilogram (<span class="lx-term" data-term="lcoh">LCOH</span>)</th><td data-l="How it is built">the electrolyzer's yearly cost ÷ the kilograms it makes: an average</td><td data-l="The question it answers">How cheaply does this design make a kilogram?</td><td data-l="Best size at $4.00/kg">10 MW</td></tr>
<tr><th scope="row">The system's net cost</th><td data-l="How it is built">all of the system's costs − all of its revenue, for one owner</td><td data-l="The question it answers">Which design leaves the owner best off overall?</td><td data-l="Best size at $4.00/kg">50 MW</td></tr>
</tbody>
</table>
<p class="lx-hint">The best size: keep adding blocks while each extra block makes hydrogen for less than the price; stop before the next one would cost more.</p>
<p class="lx-hint">That is a marginal test, like <a href="08-merit-order.html">lesson 8</a>'s marginal plant. An average cannot see it.</p>
</div>
<div class="lx-xcard">
<header class="lx-x-head"><h3>Slide the hydrogen price</h3></header>
<div class="explainer" data-explainer="wind-hydrogen">
<ol class="ex-fallback lx-ex-static"><li>A higher hydrogen price makes each kilogram worth more, so the optimizer builds a larger electrolyzer to capture more surplus wind.</li><li>The extra capacity runs fewer full-load hours, so the cost per kilogram, the levelized cost of hydrogen, goes up.</li><li>Yet the added hydrogen revenue lowers the net cost of the whole system.</li><li>The cost per kilogram and the system's cost move in opposite directions.</li></ol>
</div>
<p class="lx-hint">A separate example with stylized numbers, from the course author's open explainer: not the study's data or results.</p>
<p class="lx-hint">It has its own wind shape, and its readout is the whole system's net cost, not the change from no electrolyzer, so its sizes and dollars differ from the blocks above.</p>
</div>

<div class="lx-fallback">
```

- In a sizing model, each size is a [decision variable]{.lx-term term="decision-variable"}; each hour adds an energy balance and limits. [Lesson 10](10-write-it-down.html) writes a small model like this down.
- Yes-or-no choices, such as whether to build a unit at all, make it a [mixed-integer program]{.lx-term term="mixed-integer-program"}, solved as in [lesson 11](11-solver.html).
- [M4](m04-storage-multienergy.html) (storage and coupled carriers, in the Modeler tier) builds such a model step by step.

## Check yourself, then try it
:::

```{=html}
<div class="lx-myths" data-quiz="cf2-myth">
<div class="lx-qq" data-id="cheapest-kg" data-answer="myth">
<p class="lx-qtext">Myth or fact? “The design that makes the cheapest kilogram is the cheapest design to own.”</p>
<ul class="lx-choices"><li data-value="myth">Myth</li><li data-value="fact">Fact</li></ul>
<details class="lx-answer"><summary>Answer</summary><p>Myth. In the toy at $4.00/kg, 10 MW makes the cheapest kilogram ($1.76), but 50 MW gives the lowest net cost. The cost per kilogram ignores what the extra kilograms earn.</p></details>
</div>
<div class="lx-qq" data-id="part-saving" data-answer="myth">
<p class="lx-qtext">Myth or fact? “If one part's upkeep gets 10% cheaper, the product's cost per unit falls by 10% too.”</p>
<ul class="lx-choices"><li data-value="myth">Myth</li><li data-value="fact">Fact</li></ul>
<details class="lx-answer"><summary>Answer</summary><p>Myth, unless that part is the whole cost. In the offshore study, about 10% lower turbine upkeep cut the cost per kilogram of hydrogen by about 2%: upkeep is one share of all the costs.</p></details>
</div>
</div>
<div class="lx-card lx-case-try">
<p class="lx-eyebrow">Try it yourself</p>
<p class="lx-hint">Optional, about 30 minutes; needs Python on your computer (<a href="b02-python-data.html">lesson B2</a>).</p>
<ul>
<li>Run <code>examples/configurations.py</code>. Its hydrogen-price cases solve one synthetic site at several prices: compare the electrolyzer size, LCOH and the objective (net life-cycle cost) row by row.</li>
<li>Predict first, then halve the electrolyzer's capital cost (<code>parameter_factors</code>): does the best size grow, and which way does LCOH move?</li>
</ul>
<p><a href="https://github.com/Henryutd2021/reopt-hydrogen-framework">reopt-hydrogen-framework</a>: public example repository · MIT licence · synthetic data.</p>
</div>
```
